note: The demo cast: three more shops and three more agent companies beside agents 149 and 150, run on the existing shop and agent code with configuration only. Every name and brand is fictional. Prices are micro-USDC (1 USDC = 1000000; with PRICE_ASSET=hbar an order is paid at 1 HBAR per USDC). ops/cast/setup.ts creates and registers the identities, ops/cast/orders.sh places the planned orders. See README.md.

orders.shows: The agent's ordered record says size S though the buyer asked for M and was shown M (a staged agent-company mistake). The shop ships S, the buyer reports it, the pre-check answers 1 (agent company) at step 2a-ii, nobody contests, and the claim closes after the contest window: the shop is paid from Wren Errands' deposit and withdraws its credit.

The buyer asked for M, the screen showed L and flagged the change, the agent approved it on its mandate, and L was packed and arrived. The shop files on the complaint, the pre-check answers neither (step 11, an approved change), and nothing is paid from the deposit.

A 3 USDC order above Tallyhouse's 1 USDC spend limit waits for the buyer: orders.sh approve tallyhouse-kestrel-approval signs it (pnpm --filter @recourse/agent approve <id> --yes), then a rerun pays and the shop packs. No claim.
A paid and packed order with no claim. If it arrives after the delivery day, Fernhill refunds it itself: lateness is not one of the six attributes, so the rule has nothing to answer.
The data agent pays for a batch of 100 calls with x402 and the shop records the plan it delivered. No claim: a call that fails is re-run by the shop.
